user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my phone’s internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?

I can help you troubleshoot and improve your mobile data connection. To start, I need to identify your account and the phone line you are using. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth for verification?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.

I found three lines associated with your account. Could you please confirm which phone number you are using for the mobile data issue? The numbers are linked to your account, and I want to make sure I check the right one for data usage and connectivity.
The number I’m using is 555-123-2002—the one I mentioned earlier. That’s the phone I’m having trouble with.

Your line with phone number 555-123-2002 is active and currently has used 8.7 GB out of a 15 GB data limit for this billing cycle. Your data usage is within the plan limit, so the issue is not due to exceeding your data allowance.

Next, I will check your phone's network status and settings to diagnose why your mobile data might be slow or stopping.

To proceed with troubleshooting your mobile data issue, I need to run some diagnostic checks on your phone's network status and settings. 

Since I cannot directly access your phone, I will guide you through some checks and actions. Please confirm when you are ready, and I will provide step-by-step instructions to check your network status, mobile data settings, and other relevant configurations.
Alright, I’m ready. Please go ahead and tell me what I need to do. Just a heads up—I get a bit confused with technical stuff, so please explain things as simply as possible.

Thank you for letting me know. I'll keep the instructions simple.

First, let's check if your phone is connected to the cellular network and if mobile data is turned on.

Please do the following:
1. Look at the top of your phone screen (the status bar).
2. Check if you see any signal bars or dots indicating signal strength (like 1 to 4 bars).
3. Also, check if you see an icon that says "4G," "5G," or "LTE" near the signal bars.
4. Finally, check if there is an icon or text that says "Data Enabled" or something similar.

Let me know what you see in the status bar regarding signal bars, network type (4G/5G), and mobile data status. If you want, you can describe the icons or text you see.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I just checked, and at the top of my phone screen, I see an airplane icon, something that looks like a lock (maybe VPN?), and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything that says 4G, 5G, or LTE. Is that a problem? What should I do next?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is turned ON. This disables all wireless connections, including cellular service and mobile data, which is why you don't see any signal bars or network type.

To fix this, you need to turn Airplane Mode OFF. This will allow your phone to connect to the cellular network and enable mobile data.

Please do the following:
1. Swipe down from the top of your phone screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Look for the airplane icon in the menu.
3. Tap the airplane icon to turn Airplane Mode OFF. The icon should no longer be highlighted.

After turning off Airplane Mode, wait a few moments and check if you see signal bars and network type (4G, 5G, or LTE) appear in the status bar.

Let me know once you have done this and what you see afterward.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see one bar for signal, it says "2G," and there’s something that says "Data Disabled." I still see that lock icon and the battery at 80%. What should I do next? I really need excellent internet speed, not this 2G thing.
